──────────────────────────────────────
MILESTONE
──────────────────────────────────────
M-NODE-ACCT-1 — publish the account observation the Control Tower already parses

Objective:
The Mac Control Tower can already receive, validate, gate, project and display
a node-observed MT5 account. It has been tested offline against synthetic
payloads built only from fields `live/telemetry.py` ALREADY emits. It is
waiting for those fields to be populated.

This is not a new contract. No new schema version, no new endpoint, and no
field the Mac does not already consume.

──────────────────────────────────────
PHASE 1 — CONFIRM THE SHAPE ALREADY EXISTS
──────────────────────────────────────
Read `live/telemetry.py`:
  - `safe_identity()` builds `account.identity`
  - `safe_health()` builds `account.health`
  - `account_fingerprint(login, server)` is the one-way SHA-256 identifier
  - `_carries()` already refuses to claim `available: true` for an empty sample

Confirm both blocks are inside the existing `ct.node-telemetry.v1` envelope and
that the publisher sends them today. Report what is actually populated on a
normal cycle versus a cycle containing an OPEN.

Do not add fields. Do not change the schema version.

──────────────────────────────────────
PHASE 2 — SAMPLING CADENCE
──────────────────────────────────────
Today the node samples its account only on cycles containing an OPEN, which is
why a healthy node shows no account for long stretches.

Change the cadence so the account is sampled at least once per publish cycle,
or on a stated interval. State which you chose and why.

An account observed once a day is indistinguishable, from the Mac, from a
broken one.

──────────────────────────────────────
PHASE 3 — REQUIRED SEMANTICS
──────────────────────────────────────
MUST:
  - `account.identity.available` is a real boolean, true ONLY when the terminal
    was actually read this cycle. The Mac compares with `is True`; a missing
    key, a null, a 0 or the string "true" all read as NOT observed.
  - `account.identity` MUST accompany `account.health`. A pinned Mac deployment
    refuses a health-only observation with `account_identity_unverifiable`.
  - When `identity.available` is false, every identity field MUST be null.
    Leaving a stale fingerprint behind is the one case the Mac cannot
    distinguish from a genuine reading of that account, and it now refuses the
    whole record rather than trust the block. (`safe_identity` already does
    this. Do not regress it.)
  - `fingerprint` MUST be `account_fingerprint(login, server)`. THE RAW MT5
    LOGIN MUST NEVER BE PUBLISHED.
  - `server` MUST be the terminal's own server string, verbatim.
  - `balance` / `equity` / `free_margin` MUST be finite real numbers or null.
    NaN and Infinity are refused at ingest and the WHOLE snapshot is rejected.
    Python's own json.dumps emits a bare `Infinity` by default and json.loads
    accepts it, so no library will stop you — check before sending.
  - NEGATIVE values MUST be sent as they are. A negative balance or equity is a
    real state after a gap through a stop-out, and the Mac admits it and shows
    it with a warning. Do not clamp to zero and do not suppress the sample.
  - `null` means "not reported". It MUST NOT be used to mean zero.
  - `published_at` MUST be ISO-8601 with an explicit UTC offset, and within
    120 s of real time — the Mac FAILs activation on clock skew beyond that.

SHOULD:
  - `account.health.observed_at` — when the NODE sampled the terminal. Without
    it the Mac will never call two sources contradictory, because it cannot
    tell disagreement from drift.
  - `reconciliation.snapshot_status` reported honestly. Saying `unavailable`
    while supplying an account raises a visible contradiction warning, which is
    correct and better than claiming `ok`.
  - `cycle.status` carrying the node's own verdict. `error` or a frozen
    reconciliation makes the node DEGRADED on the Mac, which keeps the account
    visible but blocks analytics.
  - A top-level `capabilities` list containing `"account_observation"`.
    Additive, no version bump. The Mac currently cannot distinguish a new node
    that is idle from an old node that will never report, and says so as a
    permanent WARN. It will ignore this field until a Mac milestone consumes it.

MUST NOT:
  - Send a `provenance` field. The Mac derives provenance from validated
    evidence and would ignore it. A node that could declare its own authority
    would reintroduce, over the network, the exact defect the Mac's honesty
    programme removed.
  - Change `schema_version`. `ct.node-telemetry.v2` is refused with 400 and
    does not downgrade to legacy.
  - Send `available: true` with an all-null sample.
  - Publish the raw login, anywhere, in any field.

──────────────────────────────────────
PHASE 4 — FAILURE AND DEGRADED SEMANTICS
──────────────────────────────────────
When the terminal cannot be read:
  - `available: false` on both blocks, every field null
  - populate `health.reasons` with the node's own codes — the Mac displays them
    verbatim and never recomputes `healthy`

This is the ORDINARY state of a healthy node between samples, not an error.
The Mac renders it as "the node has not reported an MT5 terminal observation".

──────────────────────────────────────
PHASE 5 — TESTS
──────────────────────────────────────
Nothing here needs the Mac.

`backend/tests/activation_payloads.py` in the Control Tower repository builds
every payload class the Mac accepts and refuses. Build a snapshot that matches
`account_payload()` and passes `live_telemetry.validate_snapshot` and you have
sufficient evidence the Mac will admit it.

Test at minimum:
  - a cycle with a readable terminal produces both blocks populated
  - a cycle with an unreadable terminal produces `available: false` and ALL
    identity fields null
  - a negative equity is transmitted, not clamped or suppressed
  - no field anywhere contains the raw login
  - the fingerprint is stable across restarts for the same account

──────────────────────────────────────
PHASE 6 — LOCAL VISIBILITY
──────────────────────────────────────
Make the sampled account visible in the node's own logs or status output, at
the redaction level the node already uses (fingerprint, never login), so an
operator on the VPS can confirm what is being published without reading the
Mac.

──────────────────────────────────────
SCOPE LIMITS
──────────────────────────────────────
Do not: place orders · enable AutoTrading · leave dry_run · deploy to
production · restart or reconfigure the Mac · change the schema version · add a
new endpoint · send provenance · publish the raw login · activate anything.

──────────────────────────────────────

──────────────────────────────────────
One coherent commit. Suggested message:

Do not activate after committing. The Mac side is a separate, reviewed
procedure (`docs/governance/ACTIVATION-RUNBOOK.md`).
